tagline: Chrome extension that captures job postings and autofills applications.
verdictSummary: The tracker behind Careerflow is a small database and a board, and a personal version is a weekend. What is not a weekend is the part people actually pay for: an extension that recognises the posting layout of hundreds of job boards and applicant tracking systems, and fills their forms. A home-made extension covers the three or four sites you personally use and breaks whenever one of them ships a redesign.
coreLoopDIY: Click a button on any job posting; a browser extension reads the title, company, location and description into a local database, and a board tracks each application through applied, screening, interview and closed.
whatYouLose: form autofill across hundreds of applicant tracking systems
posting extraction that keeps working when a job board redesigns
LinkedIn profile scoring against a large sample of profiles
mock interview practice with recorded feedback
whyPeopleStillPay: Applying to fifty jobs means retyping the same twelve fields fifty times, and Careerflow removes that specific hour of tedium on sites you did not have to configure first.
notes: The interesting engineering here is not the tracker, it is keeping a scraper alive against sites that do not want to be scraped.
prompt:
Build a personal job-application tracker with two halves.

The first half is a browser extension with one button. On a job posting, it extracts title, company, location, salary if present, the posting URL and the full description text, and POSTs them to a local server. Extraction rules live in a plain JSON file — one entry per hostname, each holding CSS selectors for the fields — plus a generic fallback that reads JSON-LD `JobPosting` structured data, which a surprising number of boards publish. When neither works, the extension stores the raw page text and marks the record `needs-review` rather than saving empty fields.

The second half is a local web app over SQLite: a board with the stages applied, screening, interview, offer and closed; a card per application; and a notes field. Stage changes are stored as dated events, not as a mutable column, so the board can answer "how long did I sit in screening at each company" without extra bookkeeping. Add a follow-up view listing every application with no event for N days.

Optionally, with an LLM API key, add one action: paste your resume once, and for a selected posting produce a bullet-by-bullet rewrite suggestion with the original text shown alongside. Never rewrite the stored resume automatically — output a diff a human accepts or rejects.

Do not build form autofill for arbitrary application forms. Filling somebody else's multi-page ATS reliably is the vendor's whole product, and a half-working autofill that silently submits a wrong field is worse than typing.

faq.q: Can I import the applications I already tracked in Careerflow?
faq.a: Careerflow exports your job list as CSV, and the importer for this build is a short script: map the columns to title, company, URL, stage and date, and insert one stage event per row. What does not survive is per-posting extension metadata, because it never existed outside their extension.

For the boards you wrote selectors for, until they change their markup — usually months, sometimes weeks. The JSON-LD fallback is far more stable, so prefer boards that publish structured data. This is the honest running cost of the DIY version: about ten minutes of selector maintenance whenever a site you use redesigns.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Nothing beyond your own machine if you keep it local. The LLM rewrite step costs a fraction of a cent per posting, so a hundred tailored applications is well under a dollar.

faq.q: What is the one thing that does not survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Applying to a job you found in the wild without configuring anything first. Careerflow works on sites you have never visited; your version works on sites you taught it about.
